answers.question: Can I do all three runs next week and add the two I missed?
answers.answer: No, please do not stack the two missed runs on top of this week. After a fever that recent, the right move is to repeat the week you missed, not double it; adding runs now is the fastest way to get sick again or pick up a niggle. You still have 8 weeks to the race, which is plenty of runway if we stay steady.

new.analysis:
## How the week went
You followed Monday as planned, then the cold and fever took Wednesday and Saturday, and that is the right call. One short walk-run after a 38.4 fever is a sensible return, not a failure.

## Why this plan
We repeat the week you missed rather than add to it, because your lungs and legs have had almost no load for 10 days. Monday is a touch shorter so you can see how the cough behaves under effort before Wednesday.

## What I am watching
Keep every run at a conversational effort, around 6/10, and if the cough gets worse during or after a run, stop and walk home. If the plan feels easy by Saturday, that is good news we will use next week, not this one.

safetyCallouts.title: Returning after a fever.
safetyCallouts.body: You had a 38.4 fever ending Fri Sep 11 and are still coughing. If the cough worsens, you get chest pain or tightness, breathlessness out of proportion to the effort, a racing heart at rest, or the fever comes back, stop running and see your GP before the next session. Do not push through a chest infection.
